title: Dedicated cluster pulse & burst composer — console UX prototype
creator: Asha Raman
description: Design and prototype a consolidated Dedicated Capacity view that surfaces cluster-level health signals, autoscaling controls, and burst configuration in a single compact canvas. The goal is to give SREs and platform engineers a fast way to triage capacity issues, tune autoscale policies, and initiate controlled bursts without diving into multiple screens. This ticket covers low-fidelity -> high-fidelity prototypes, a lightweight usability test with two customers, and a design review with Eng + PM.
acceptance_criteria: Single-screen mock that shows: live capacity utilization sparkline, queue depth histogram, avg latency by model, current autoscale policy, and burst toggle with confirmation flow
Interactive prototype (Figma) with toggles for: policy edit, manual burst + duration, canary-burst option, and preview of cost delta
Handoff-ready spec for engineering including spacing tokens, interaction notes, and accessibility contrast checks
Usability test summary with <=3 major usability issues and recommended mitigations
Design review sign-off from PM (Elena Torres) and Eng lead (Ravi Patel)
mockups: Canvas Overview: frame 1 - compact header with cluster selector and health summary
Triage Mode: frame 2 - focus on queue depth, node-level alerts, and suggested remediations
Autoscale Composer: frame 3 - visual policy editor with instant preview of throughput impact
Burst Flow: frame 4 - confirm modal, cost estimate, canary toggle, rollback timer
feedback: Elena Torres (PM) — Prefer a cost-first callout in the burst flow; customers asked for immediate cost delta before confirming
Ravi Patel (Eng) — Kernel scheduling metrics would be useful but may not be available from the runtime API; recommend placeholder with link to infra metrics
Design critique (internal) — Consider collapsing 'node list' into an expandable panel to reduce visual noise on first glance
Customer test (ACME AI) — Liked single-screen approach; confused by 'canary burst' wording — suggested 'staged burst' instead
comments: 2026-02-19 — Asha Raman: Initial low-fi sketches uploaded to Figma. Focused on three states: healthy, warning, critical. Tagged ENG and PM for early feedback.
2026-02-22 — Marco Valdez: Iterated to include queue depth histogram and a compact per-model latency sparkline. Added keyboard-accessible controls for burst toggle.
2026-02-25 — Elena Torres (PM): Requested visible SLAs per cluster and a link to rollout history. Added as dependency for ENG-91200.
2026-02-28 — Usability test run with two customers (ACME AI, FinTech Co). Collected session recordings and transcript. Summary attached to Drive.
2026-03-01 — Marco Valdez: Updated hi-fi with color ramp for health states and added ARIA labels. Ready for design review on 2026-03-03.
decisions: Use a compact single-row header: cluster selector + health dot + latency summary + action menu
Autoscale policy editing will be in-line with an 'apply preview' step rather than a separate wizard to reduce context switching
Burst initiation requires two-step confirmation with explicit cost delta and an optional canary/staged toggle
Expose a lightweight 'suggested remediation' CTA powered by runtime heuristics, but require Eng work item to populate signals (ENG-90210)
Accessibility: ensure 4.5:1 contrast on interactive elements and provide keyboard-only workflows for all controls
next_steps: Incorporate feedback from design review on 2026-03-03; update Figma frames accordingly
Create engineering ticket with annotated spec and tokenized spacing/colors (ENG-95290)
Add instrumentation hooks for cost preview (work with Billing team) — PM to coordinate
Run follow-up usability test focused on the burst confirmation flow wording (staged vs canary)
Prepare handoff package with Motion specs for autoscale policy transitions
risks: Showing cost deltas without accurate billing hooks may lead to incorrect user decisions — mitigation: show 'estimated' label and link to billing docs
Too much information on a single canvas risks overwhelming new users — mitigation: progressive disclosure and default collapsed node list
Runtime signal availability mismatch (kernel scheduling metrics) — mitigation: placeholder rows with link to infra dashboards and expedite ENG dependency
accessibility_notes: All interactive controls include ARIA labels. Color palette adjusted to meet 4.5:1 contrast on key CTAs. Tested keyboard-only flows for policy editor and burst confirmation. Need Eng signoff for focus management when preview panels open.
